key_insight: Chatter Attack induces short, doubt-triggering phrases that can steer LLMs into prolonged responses, amplifying inference resource consumption.
engineering_relevance: The attack highlights availability and cost risks for LLM services, motivating output-token limits, generation timeouts, and resource monitoring.
method: Optimize adversarial prompts toward short doubt-inducing target phrases rather than entire long responses.
Use inference attention loss and global entropy loss to sustain self-doubt during generation.
Extend to black-box settings with Bayesian Prompt Optimization using a discrete token kernel.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experiments across multiple models and datasets, outperforming baselines with response-length increases of up to 31.5×.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify black-box query costs or whether effectiveness persists under strict output-token and time limits.
paper_title: Chatter Attack: Resource Consumption Attack for Large Language Models
